title: Asking for a break when I need one
examples: How do I ask for a break?
What if I need a break in class?

explain.say: Imagine a kettle getting hotter and hotter. If the steam cannot get out, it whistles loudly! Feelings can be like that. Look at the board. On the left, holding it in. On the right, asking for a break.

draw.text: Asking for a break when I need one

explain.say: See the left side? Holding it in. The feeling gets bigger. Your grown-up does not know. And it is hard to learn. Have you ever held a feeling in until it got too big?

Now the right side. Asking for a break. Your grown-up can help. You get a short calm break. Then you come back, ready to learn. Asking is like letting a little steam out of the kettle. Which side feels better?
Here are the steps. Notice your body feels too full. Then ask. See the speech bubble? You can say, Can I have a break, please? Take a few calm minutes, then come back. Can you say the words with me?

explain.say: There are many ways to ask. With words: A break, please? I need a minute. Can I get water? Without words: a break card, a hand signal, or pointing to a picture. Brilliant! Your challenge: choose your way to ask.

faq.q: What words can I use to ask for a break?
faq.a: You can say, Can I have a break, please? or I need a minute, please. Short and calm is perfect.

faq.q: How do I know I need a break?
faq.a: Check your body. Hot face, tight fists, wiggly legs or a full head are signs. Ask early, before the feeling gets too big.

faq.q: What if my teacher says not now?
faq.a: Your teacher might say, In two minutes. Take a slow breath and wait. If it is very hard, you can say, I really need it, please. A grown-up you trust can help you make a plan.
It is a small card you can show your teacher when talking feels hard. It means, I need a break, please.

faq.q: Why is holding feelings in hard?
faq.a: Feelings grow when they have nowhere to go. A short break lets them settle, like letting steam out of a kettle.

facts: Many schools use break cards so children can ask for a break without words.
A short break can help people return to work feeling calmer.
